title: The AI Content System Behind 200M Views — Sarah Chieng, Cerebras & Cova Lee, OpenAI
talk_summary: A content-creation workshop by Cerebras and OpenAI DevRel staff showing how they use fast models, custom-built tools, swipe files, and reusable 'skills' to systematize video ideation, scripting, editing, and publishing. Most content is creator-workflow specific, but a few mechanisms (skill libraries, self-review of process, custom research tools, outlier analysis) transfer to agent orchestration.

takeaways.technique: Hierarchical skill library with process checklist
takeaways.what_they_do: They maintain one master skill per tool/domain (e.g. Premiere) with sub-skills for each step, plus an ordered process list so the agent knows which steps are done and what's next, and they continuously prune/update it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I have everything in there for like color grading, sound effects. I have a caption skill ... it has like this process list of like 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 to like 12.

takeaways.technique: Weekly self-review of process to find automation candidates
takeaways.what_they_do: They run a recurring skill that reviews their own workflow logs, surfaces where time is spent, and suggests repetitive tasks to turn into tools or drop entirely.
takeaways.evidence_quote: review my video creation process. Show me where I spend the most time and suggest repetitive tasks I could turn into tools or automate.

takeaways.technique: Build custom research/analysis tools before doing the work
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of doing tasks manually, they prompt agents to build small bespoke tools (e.g. a YouTube outlier finder with a 1x-20x slider) to understand the domain before committing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one of the best things about agents is it allows you to be able to build custom tools for understanding how you can build things before you go ahead doing them.

takeaways.what_they_do: They compare results relative to a baseline (outlier theory, engagement vs. channel average) rather than absolute numbers, and explicitly ask the model to do this.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's specifically designed to find outliers. Like it has a slider that goes from like 1x to like 20x the normal like average views on that channel.

takeaways.what_they_do: They paste a known list of AI-writing tells into the prompt and instruct the model to avoid everything on it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's this like article on Wikipedia that's called like signs of AI writing and I will always just paste it in and be like, do not do anything that is mentioned in here.
